minutes.headline: Assessors voted 2-0 to appoint Select Board member Lou Franco as temporary meeting moderator, then went to executive session.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a dispute over whether and how a Select Board member could moderate the Board of Assessors during the lakefront property tax controversy. A motion to appoint Lou Franco was moved, seconded, amended (deleting a sentence limiting his speaking) and passed. Two residents spoke in public comment about executive session access and the land value increase calculation, and the board then entered executive session.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors passed a motion, 2-0 as heard, appointing Select Board member Lou Franco temporary moderator for meetings on the lakefront tax situation.
The board amended the motion 2-1 to delete a sentence limiting the moderator to responding only with the chair's permission.
With the amendment, the moderator may answer public questions directly; public comment was limited to two named speakers at about five minutes each.
A resident formally asked the board to direct the principal assessor to explain how the land value increase for lake properties was calculated.
The board approved prior minutes, then entered executive session by roll call.

why_it_matters: The lakefront assessment dispute affects the property tax bills of lake homeowners, and who runs the meeting shapes how residents can question the assessors.
Residents asked how the land value increase for lake properties was calculated and whether abatement applicants may attend discussion of their cases, and the minutes record no answer to either.
watch_next: Whether the board directs the principal assessor to publish the calculation of the lake property land value increase.
When the board decides in public whether abatement applicants may attend discussion of their applications.
